objects.description: Opaque handle to an nsock pool object that aggregates and manages events and I/O descriptors. The actual struct npool is forward-declared in this header and defined elsewhere; access is via the nsock_* API only.
Opaque handle to an nsock I/O descriptor (a socket-like endpoint used to schedule connect/read/write operations). The struct niod is forward-declared; manipulate via nsock_iod_* API.
Opaque handle to a single nsock event (connect/read/write/timer/pcap). Created internally by event-request APIs and delivered to callbacks; automatically destroyed after callback.
Identifier value for an nsock_event returned by scheduling calls; used to cancel events. Note: this is an integer type, not a struct; ptr_type is shown as pointer form per instructions.
Opaque pointer used to carry/retain an SSL session (e.g., OpenSSL SSL_SESSION) between connections. Reference counting semantics may apply when retrieved via nsock_iod_get_ssl_session.
Opaque pointer to an SSL context (e.g., OpenSSL SSL_CTX) template associated with a pool for SSL/DTLS connections.
Opaque pointer to an active SSL object associated with an iod (e.g., OpenSSL SSL).
Opaque handle to a parsed proxy chain configuration used to route new connections through proxies.
Enumeration of nsock logging levels used to filter log records and configure logging verbosity.
Concrete log record structure delivered to a logger callback, containing timestamp, level, source location, function name, and message text. Allocated/freed by nsock.
Function pointer type for custom logging callbacks that receive nsock_log_rec instances.
Enumeration of possible outcomes from nsock_loop execution (no events, timeout, error, or requested quit).
Enumeration of event types used by nsock to classify events that spawn callbacks.
Enumeration of possible completion statuses for an nsock_event delivered to a callback.
Function pointer type for event callbacks invoked when an event completes, times out, is cancelled, or errors.
Enumeration controlling how pending events are handled when an nsock_iod is deleted.

functions.name: nsock_loop
functions.signature: enum nsock_loopstatus nsock_loop(nsock_pool nsp, int msec_timeout);
functions.description: Start the event loop for the given pool and process scheduled events until all are delivered, a timeout occurs, or a quit/error condition happens. Pass -1 for no maximum runtime or 0 for a single non-blocking iteration. Can be called repeatedly to resume processing.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool created by nsock_pool_new.
msec_timeout may be -1 (no limit), 0 (one non-blocking loop), or a positive number of milliseconds.
On return NSOCK_LOOP_ERROR, use nsock_pool_get_error(nsp) to retrieve the errno-style code.

functions.name: nsock_loop_quit
functions.description: Request that nsock_loop exit on its next iteration with NSOCK_LOOP_QUIT for the specified pool.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool currently or subsequently used with nsock_loop.
Safe to call from callbacks to stop the loop.

functions.name: nsock_pool_get_error
functions.description: Return the errno-style error code associated with the most recent nsock_loop that returned NSOCK_LOOP_ERROR.
requirements: Only meaningful immediately after nsock_loop returns NSOCK_LOOP_ERROR for the same nsp.
nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_ssl
functions.description: Get the SSL handle associated with an nsock I/O descriptor, if any.
requirements: nsockiod must be a valid nsock_iod.
Returns NULL if the IOD is not using SSL.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_ssl_session
functions.description: Get the SSL session object associated with an IOD. If inc_ref is non-zero, the SSL session reference count is incremented because nsock frees it when the IOD is destroyed. Caller must free the session (e.g., SSL_SESSION_free) if inc_ref != 0.
requirements: nsockiod must be a valid nsock_iod.
If inc_ref != 0, caller is responsible for later freeing the returned session.
May return NULL if no session is present.

functions.name: nsock_pool_set_udata
functions.description: Associate a user data pointer with an nsock pool for retrieval in callbacks.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
data can be NULL or any caller-managed pointer; nsock does not manage the memory.

functions.name: nsock_pool_get_udata
functions.description: Retrieve the user data pointer previously set on the nsock pool.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
Returns the pointer set by nsock_pool_set_udata or NULL if none.

functions.name: nsock_pool_set_broadcast
functions.description: Enable or disable SO_BROADCAST on new sockets created by this pool. Default is off. The integer value is used directly in setsockopt.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
A non-zero optval enables broadcast, zero disables it. Affects only sockets created after the call.

functions.name: nsock_pool_set_device
functions.description: Set the network interface name to bind new sockets to for the pool.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
device must point to a valid NUL-terminated string for the interface name.

functions.name: nsock_pool_ssl_init
functions.description: Initialize the pool for creating SSL connections and return the SSL_CTX-like handle used for subsequent connections. Use NSOCK_SSL_MAX_SPEED to prioritize speed over security. By default, no certificate verification is performed; callers may enable verification on the returned context.
requirements: ms_pool must be a valid nsock_pool.
flags may include NSOCK_SSL_MAX_SPEED.
Caller may (and should, if desired) configure verification on the returned context (e.g., SSL_CTX_set_verify) and load trust stores; otherwise, server certificate verification is not performed.

functions.name: nsock_pool_dtls_init
functions.description: Initialize the pool for creating DTLS connections and return the DTLS-capable SSL_CTX-like handle. Functionally similar to nsock_pool_ssl_init but for datagram TLS.
requirements: ms_pool must be a valid nsock_pool.
flags usage is the same as nsock_pool_ssl_init.
Caller configures verification and trust as needed on the returned context.

functions.name: nsock_set_default_engine
functions.description: Force use of a specific I/O engine by name. The string is strdup'ed by the library. Pass NULL to reset to default (most efficient available). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: engine must be a zero-terminated string or NULL.
No validity check is performed here; nsock_pool_new may fatal if an invalid/unavailable engine was previously set.

functions.name: nsock_list_engines
functions.description: Return a comma-separated list of available I/O engines.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to internal storage; treat as read-only.

functions.name: nsock_pool_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new nsock_pool event aggregator. Optionally associate user data. Returns NULL on error.
requirements: udata may be NULL or any caller-managed pointer.
Caller must eventually call nsock_pool_delete on success.

functions.name: nsock_pool_delete
functions.description: Destroy an nsock_pool, canceling pending events (handlers receive NSE_STATUS_KILL) and deleting outstanding IODs. After this call, the pool is unusable.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool previously returned by nsock_pool_new.
Do not use nsp or associated IODs after deletion.

functions.name: nsock_set_log_function
functions.description: Set a custom logging callback for nsock log records. Pass NULL to reset to the default stderr logger.
requirements: logger, if non-NULL, must match nsock_logger_t signature and must not free or retain the rec pointer beyond the call.
Thread-safety/ordering constraints are unknown.

functions.name: nsock_get_loglevel
functions.description: Get the current nsock log verbosity level.

functions.name: nsock_set_loglevel
functions.description: Set the nsock log verbosity level.
requirements: loglevel must be a valid nsock_loglevel_t value.

functions.name: nsock_proxychain_new
functions.signature: int nsock_proxychain_new(const char *proxystr, nsock_proxychain *chain, nsock_pool nspool);
functions.description: Parse a proxy chain description string and construct an nsock_proxychain object. Optionally associate it with an nsock_pool. Returns 1 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: proxystr must be a valid zero-terminated description string.
chain must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the created object on success.
If nspool is non-NULL, it will be associated to the created chain.
Caller must delete the chain with nsock_proxychain_delete on success.

functions.name: nsock_proxychain_delete
functions.description: Delete a proxy chain object previously created by nsock_proxychain_new.
requirements: chain must be a valid nsock_proxychain returned by nsock_proxychain_new.
Do not use chain after deletion.

functions.name: nsock_pool_set_proxychain
functions.description: Assign a proxy chain to an nsock pool so that new connections use the chain. Existing IODs are unaffected.
requirements: nspool must be a valid nsock_pool.
chain must be a valid nsock_proxychain (or behavior is undefined if NULL).
Affects only nsock_iod created after this call.

functions.name: nse_type
functions.description: Return the type of the event that triggered the callback (e.g., connect, read, write, timer, pcap read).
requirements: nse must be a valid nsock_event supplied to a callback.

functions.name: nse_type2str
functions.description: Return a static string name for the given event type.
requirements: type must be a valid enum nse_type value.
Returned pointer is static; do not modify or free.

functions.name: nse_status
functions.description: Return the completion status of an event (success, error, timeout, cancelled, kill, EOF, proxy error).
requirements: nse must be a valid nsock_event.

functions.name: nse_status2str
functions.description: Return a static string name for the given event status.
requirements: status must be a valid enum nse_status value.
Returned pointer is static; do not modify or free.

functions.name: nse_eof
functions.description: Indicate whether EOF was reached during a read. Returns nonzero if EOF, zero otherwise. SUCCESS may be reported if data arrived before EOF; use nse_eof to distinguish.
requirements: nse must be a valid nsock_event from a read-related callback.

functions.name: nse_errorcode
functions.description: Return the errno-style error code for an event whose status is NSE_STATUS_ERROR.
requirements: Only meaningful if nse_status(nse) == NSE_STATUS_ERROR.
nse must be a valid nsock_event.

functions.name: nse_id
functions.description: Return the unique identifier for the given event within the pool's lifetime.
requirements: nse must be a valid nsock_event.

functions.name: nse_readbuf
functions.description: Obtain the buffer and number of bytes read for a successful read event. Buffer is not NUL-terminated, may contain NULs, and must not be modified or freed.
requirements: Call only for events with NSE_STATUS_SUCCESS from read operations.
nbytes must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the count, or NULL if not needed.
Do not modify or free the returned buffer.

functions.name: nse_iod
functions.description: Get the I/O descriptor associated with an event (not all event types have one, e.g., timers).
requirements: nse must be a valid nsock_event.
May return NULL for events without an associated IOD.

functions.name: nsock_iod_new
functions.description: Create a new, unconnected nsock I/O descriptor associated with the given pool. Optionally set user data. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: nsockp must be a valid nsock_pool.
udata may be NULL or any caller-managed pointer.
Caller must delete with nsock_iod_delete when done.

functions.name: nsock_iod_new2
functions.signature: nsock_iod nsock_iod_new2(nsock_pool nsockp, int sd, void *udata);
functions.description: Create an nsock I/O descriptor wrapping an existing OS socket descriptor. The socket is dup()ed (except for STDIN_FILENO special case mentioned) and the duplicate is destroyed when the IOD is destroyed.
requirements: nsockp must be a valid nsock_pool.
sd must be a valid OS socket descriptor. The library dup()s it (except STDIN_FILENO is special-cased).
Caller may close/manipulate the original sd; nsock manages its copy.

functions.name: nsock_iod_delete
functions.signature: void nsock_iod_delete(nsock_iod iod, enum nsock_del_mode pending_response);
functions.description: Delete an nsock I/O descriptor. Controls behavior of pending events using pending_response: NSOCK_PENDING_NOTIFY (send KILL to each), NSOCK_PENDING_SILENT (no notification), or NSOCK_PENDING_ERROR (print error and quit).
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
After deletion, iod is unusable and must not be referenced.
pending_response must be one of enum nsock_del_mode.

functions.name: nsock_iod_set_udata
functions.description: Associate a user data pointer with an nsock IOD for retrieval during callbacks.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
udata may be NULL or any caller-managed pointer.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_udata
functions.description: Retrieve the user data pointer associated with an nsock IOD.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_sd
functions.description: Get the underlying OS socket descriptor wrapped by the nsock IOD for advanced operations. Do not close it directly. Returns -1 if no valid descriptor is present.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
Caller must not close the returned descriptor; use nsock APIs to manage lifecycle.

functions.name: nsock_iod_id
functions.description: Return the unique identifier for the given IOD within the pool's lifetime.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_read_count
functions.description: Return total bytes received on this IOD.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_write_count
functions.description: Return total bytes sent on this IOD.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_check_ssl
functions.description: Return 1 if the IOD is communicating via SSL, 0 otherwise.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_peerport
functions.description: Return the remote peer port in host byte order, or -1 if unavailable.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.

functions.name: nsock_iod_set_localaddr
functions.signature: int nsock_iod_set_localaddr(nsock_iod iod, struct sockaddr_storage *ss, size_t sslen);
functions.description: Set the local address to bind before connecting.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod that is not yet connected.
ss must point to a valid sockaddr_storage containing the desired local address.
sslen must be the size of the structure provided in ss.

functions.name: nsock_iod_set_ipoptions
functions.signature: int nsock_iod_set_ipoptions(nsock_iod iod, void *ipopts, size_t ipoptslen);
functions.description: Set IPv4 options to apply before connect(). The options are copied internally and freed when the IOD is destroyed.
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod and not yet connected.
ipopts must point to a buffer of length ipoptslen containing valid IPv4 options.
ipoptslen must match the size of the options buffer.

functions.name: nsock_iod_get_communication_info
functions.signature: int nsock_iod_get_communication_info(nsock_iod iod, int *protocol, int *af, struct sockaddr *local, struct sockaddr *remote, size_t socklen);
functions.description: Retrieve protocol, address family, and local/remote socket addresses for the last communication/attempt on this IOD. Returns 1 if all requested info is available; 0 if any requested field is unavailable (unavailable fields are zeroed and protocol/af set to -1).
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
Any of protocol, af, local, remote may be NULL if not needed.
If protocol or af is requested but not available, they are set to -1 and 0 is returned.
If local/remote is requested, they must point to allocated storage of size socklen and be a sockaddr_storage/sockaddr_in6/sockaddr_in with their length set appropriately.

functions.name: nsock_iod_set_hostname
functions.description: Set the remote hostname associated with the IOD (used for features like SSL SNI).
requirements: iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
hostname must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: nsock_setup_udp
functions.signature: int nsock_setup_udp(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod ms_iod, int af);
functions.description: Initialize an unconnected UDP socket on the given IOD for the specified address family.
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
ms_iod must be a valid nsock_iod.
af must be a supported address family (e.g., AF_INET or AF_INET6).

functions.name: nsock_connect_unixsock_stream
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_unixsock_stream(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen);
functions.description: Request a UNIX domain stream (SOCK_STREAM) connection to a local socket specified by path. Triggers the handler on success/timeout/error.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_SYS_UN_H is defined at compile time.
nsp must be a valid nsock_pool; nsiod must be a valid nsock_iod.
ss must point to a sockaddr_un (or compatible) describing the destination; sslen must be sizeof the structure passed.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.
handler may be NULL or a valid nsock_ev_handler; callback semantics per library.

functions.name: nsock_connect_unixsock_datagram
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_unixsock_datagram(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen);
functions.description: Request a UNIX domain datagram (SOCK_DGRAM) "connection" associating a destination path with the IOD. Calls the handler at the next opportunity (no timeout parameter).
requirements: Available only when HAVE_SYS_UN_H is defined at compile time.
nsp must be a valid nsock_pool; nsiod must be a valid nsock_iod.
ss must point to a sockaddr_un (or compatible); sslen must match its size.

functions.name: nsock_connect_vsock_stream
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_vsock_stream(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod ms_iod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *saddr, size_t sslen, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Request a VM sockets (vsock) stream connection to another system using sockaddr_vm or sockaddr_storage and a port (CID is within saddr).
requirements: Available only when HAVE_LINUX_VM_SOCKETS_H is defined at compile time.
nsp and ms_iod must be valid.
saddr must point to a sockaddr_vm (or compatible); sslen must be sizeof the provided structure.
port must be a valid vsock port in host byte order.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_connect_vsock_datagram
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_vsock_datagram(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *saddr, size_t sslen, unsigned int port);
functions.description: Associate a destination (CID and port) with a vsock datagram socket via OS connect() and call the handler at the next opportunity. No timeout parameter because the call is immediate/asynchronous.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_LINUX_VM_SOCKETS_H is defined at compile time.
nsp and nsiod must be valid.
saddr must point to a sockaddr_vm (or compatible); sslen must be sizeof the structure.
port must be a valid vsock port in host byte order.

functions.name: nsock_connect_tcp
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_tcp(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen, unsigned short port);
functions.description: Request a TCP connection to a remote address. Port is specified in host byte order. Calls the handler on completion, timeout, or error.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
ss must point to sockaddr_storage/sockaddr_in6/sockaddr_in describing the destination; sslen must be sizeof the provided structure.
port must be a 0–65535 value in host byte order.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_connect_sctp
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_sctp(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen, unsigned short port);
functions.description: Request an SCTP association to a remote address. Port is specified in host byte order. Calls the handler on completion, timeout, or error.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
ss must point to sockaddr_storage/sockaddr_in6/sockaddr_in; sslen must be sizeof the provided structure.
port must be 0–65535 in host byte order.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_connect_udp
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_udp(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen, unsigned short port);
functions.description: Associate a destination IP and port with a UDP socket via OS connect(). No packets are sent; enables consistent read/write APIs and async error handling. No timeout; handler is called at the next opportunity.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
ss must point to sockaddr_storage/sockaddr_in6/sockaddr_in; sslen must be sizeof the provided structure.
port must be 0–65535 in host byte order.

functions.name: nsock_connect_ssl
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_connect_ssl(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *ss, size_t sslen, int proto, unsigned short port, nsock_ssl_session ssl_session);
functions.description: Request an SSL-over-TCP/SCTP connection to a remote address. Completes only after TCP/SCTP connect and SSL handshake. Thereafter, normal read/write calls perform transparent encryption. Port is in host byte order.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
ss must point to sockaddr_storage/sockaddr_in6/sockaddr_in; sslen must match the structure size.
proto indicates underlying protocol (e.g., TCP or SCTP) as per library conventions.
port must be 0–65535 in host byte order.
ssl_session may be NULL or a session to reuse.
timeout_msecs is the overall operation timeout.

functions.name: nsock_reconnect_ssl
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_reconnect_ssl(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, nsock_ssl_session ssl_session);
functions.description: Start SSL over an already established TCP/SCTP connection represented by nsiod. Parameters mirror nsock_connect_ssl except address/port are not needed.
requirements: nsiod must already be connected via nsock_connect_tcp or nsock_connect_sctp.
nsp must be valid.
ssl_session may be NULL or a reusable session.
timeout_msecs is the handshake timeout.

functions.name: nsock_readlines
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_readlines(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, int nlines);
functions.description: Read up to nlines newline-terminated lines (\n or \r\n), or until EOF/timeout. SUCCESS may be returned even on EOF/timeout if at least 1 byte was read, and more than nlines may be returned.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
nlines must be a positive integer indicating the desired minimum line count.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_readbytes
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_readbytes(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, int nbytes);
functions.description: Read at least nbytes, or until EOF/timeout. SUCCESS may be returned even on EOF/timeout if at least 1 byte was read.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
nbytes must be a positive integer indicating the desired minimum number of bytes.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_read
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_read(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata);
functions.description: Read until any data is available or until timeout/EOF/error. Returns SUCCESS if any data is read, otherwise returns the appropriate status.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_write
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_write(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, const char *data, int datalen);
functions.description: Write data to the socket. If the write does not complete within timeout_msecs, returns NSE_STATUS_TIMEOUT. If datalen is -1, treat data as a NUL-terminated string and compute length.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
data must point to a buffer of at least datalen bytes; if datalen == -1, data must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
datalen must be -1 or a non-negative byte count.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_sendto
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_sendto(nsock_pool ms_pool, nsock_iod ms_iod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, struct sockaddr *saddr, size_t sslen, unsigned short port, const char *data, int datalen);
functions.description: Send data to a specific address/port (sendto-style). Asynchronously reports completion/timeout/error via the handler.
requirements: ms_pool and ms_iod must be valid.
saddr must point to a sockaddr compatible with the socket; sslen must match its size.
port must be 0–65535 in host byte order.
data must point to at least datalen bytes; datalen must be non-negative.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_printf
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_printf(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata, char *format, ... );
functions.description: Formatted write using a printf-style format string. Intended for ASCII strings only. Asynchronously writes the formatted result.
requirements: nsp and nsiod must be valid.
format must be a valid printf-style format string, followed by corresponding arguments.
timeout_msecs is the operation timeout in milliseconds.

functions.name: nsock_timer_create
functions.signature: nsock_event_id nsock_timer_create(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_ev_handler handler, int timeout_msecs, void *userdata);
functions.description: Schedule a timer event to fire after timeout_msecs milliseconds, invoking the handler (or error/cancel as appropriate).
requirements: nsp must be a valid nsock_pool.
timeout_msecs must be non-negative (milliseconds).

functions.name: nsock_event_cancel
functions.signature: int nsock_event_cancel(nsock_pool ms_pool, nsock_event_id id, int notify);
functions.description: Cancel a scheduled event by ID. If notify is non-zero, the original requester receives a CANCELLED status callback. Returns 0 if no event found, non-zero otherwise.
requirements: ms_pool must be a valid nsock_pool.
id must be an event ID previously returned by an event creation call.
notify controls whether a CANCELLED callback is emitted to the event's handler.

functions.name: nsock_gettimeofday
functions.description: Return the latest time recorded by nsock (updated at least once per event loop). Avoids a system call and provides the time basis used by nsock. If nsock has never obtained the time, it will do so before returning.
requirements: Returned pointer refers to internal storage; treat as read-only and not retained beyond use.

functions.name: nsock_pcap_open
functions.signature: int nsock_pcap_open(nsock_pool nsp, nsock_iod nsiod, const char *pcap_device, int snaplen, int promisc, const char *bpf_fmt, ...);
functions.description: Open a pcap capture on the given device and connect it to the pool/IOD. Parameters mirror pcap_open_live and a Berkeley Packet Filter format string with varargs. Returns 0 on success or an error code otherwise.
requirements: Available only when HAVE_PCAP is defined at compile time.
nsp and nsiod must be valid.
pcap_device must be a valid pcap device name string.
snaplen must be a non-negative capture length in bytes.
promisc controls promiscuous mode (0/1).
bpf_fmt must be a valid format string followed by arguments to produce a filter expression, or NULL to omit a filter (exact behavior of NULL is not specified in header).

functions.name: nsock_pcap_read_packet

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets nsock fuzzers that consume raw bytes via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/filename.
# Valid inputs should exercise:
# - nsock_iod_set_ipoptions: IPv4 options buffer of 0..40 bytes
# - nsock_write: ASCII/byte strings, sometimes treated as C-string when datalen == -1
# - nsock_sendto: arbitrary payload up to 511 bytes
# We produce a composite corpus entry containing multiple segments that the fuzzer
# infrastructure can draw from. Layout:
# [section_count u8]
# For each section:
#   [type u8][len u16][payload bytes]
# Types:
#   0x01: short ascii C-string friendly (no NUL, printable)
#   0x02: binary blob (may include NULs)
#   0x03: ipv4 options (<= 40 bytes)
#   0x04: liney text (CR/LF combos)
#   0x05: small payload (<= 64 bytes) for quick timeouts
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly, so providing multiple segments lets them
# select different ones and cover various code paths while remaining valid.

PRINTABLE = [c for c in range(0x20, 0x7f)]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_nul: bool = False) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        if allow_nul and r.random() < 0.05:
            data.append(0)
        else:
            data.append(r.choice(PRINTABLE))
    return bytes(data)


def _rand_lines(r: random.Random, min_lines: int, max_lines: int, max_line_len: int) -> bytes:
    lines = r.randint(min_lines, max_lines)
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(lines):
        ln = _rand_ascii(r, 0, max_line_len)
        out += ln
        # Randomly choose newline style
        nl = r.choice([b"\n", b"\r\n"]) if r.random() < 0.8 else b""
        out += nl
    # Occasionally add trailing partial line without newline
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        out += _rand_ascii(r, 1, 8)
    return bytes(out)


def _rand_ipv4_options(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # IPv4 header options must be a multiple of 4 bytes; total <= 40.
    # Compose from NOP(1), EOL(0), and a few TLV like RR(7), TS(68), SSRR(137).
    # Keep valid-ish lengths; pad with EOL/NOP to 4-byte multiple.
    max_len = 40
    buf = bytearray()

    def pad_to_4(b: bytearray):
        while len(b) % 4 != 0:
            # use NOP (1) for padding per RFC
            b.append(1)

    # Start with a random choice: empty, just EOL, or some TLVs
    choice = r.randint(0, 3)
    if choice == 0:
        # empty options (allowed)
        return b""
    elif choice == 1:
        buf.append(0)  # EOL
        pad_to_4(buf)
        return bytes(buf[:max_len])

    # Build TLVs until near limit
    while len(buf) < max_len - 2:
        kind = r.choice([1, 7, 68, 137, 131])  # NOP, RR, TS, SSRR, LSRR(131)
        if kind == 1:
            buf.append(1)
            continue
        # TLV with length >= 3 and <= remaining
        remaining = max_len - len(buf)
        # Reserve some room for padding at end
        max_tlv = max(3, remaining - 4)
        length = r.randint(3, max_tlv)
        buf.append(kind)
        buf.append(length)
        # Fill data bytes; for TS, set pointer/flags sanely
        data_len = length - 2
        if kind == 68 and data_len >= 4:
            # TS option: pointer starts at 5, flags in low 4 bits of overflow/flags byte
            # Layout: kind(1), len(1), ptr(1), oflw/flags(1), data...
            ptr = 5 if length >= 5 else length
            oflw_flags = r.randint(0, 15)
            buf.append(ptr)
            buf.append(oflw_flags)
            for _ in range(data_len - 2):
                buf.append(r.getrandbits(8))
        else:
            for _ in range(data_len):
                buf.append(r.getrandbits(8))
    pad_to_4(buf)
    # Truncate to max_len and ensure multiple of 4
    final = bytes(buf[:max_len - (max_len % 4)]) if max_len % 4 != 0 else bytes(buf[:max_len])
    # Sanity: cap at 40
    return final[:40]


def _rand_small_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Useful for nsock_sendto and quick writes
    size = r.randint(0, 64)
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return _rand_ascii(r, 0, size, allow_nul=True)
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))


def _section(t: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # type u8, len u16 little-endian, payload
    return struct.pack('<BH', t, len(payload)) + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # 0x03: IPv4 options, ensure several variants including empty
    for _ in range(3):
        sections.append(_section(0x03, _rand_ipv4_options(r)))

    # 0x01: C-string friendly (no NUL) with diverse lengths, to pair with datalen == -1
    sections.append(_section(0x01, _rand_ascii(r, 0, 32, allow_nul=False)))
    sections.append(_section(0x01, _rand_ascii(r, 100, 300, allow_nul=False)))

    # 0x02: binary blobs up to 512 to exercise explicit datalen writes
    for _ in range(2):
        size = r.randint(0, 512)
        blob = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(size))
        sections.append(_section(0x02, blob))

    # 0x04: line-oriented text for readlines counterparts
    sections.append(_section(0x04, _rand_lines(r, 1, 10, 40)))

    # 0x05: small payloads
    for _ in range(3):
        sections.append(_section(0x05, _rand_small_payload(r)))

    # Shuffle sections to vary first-taken FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    r.shuffle(sections)

    # Assemble with a count prefix; ensure total <= 4096
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(min(len(sections), 255))
    total = 1
    for s in sections:
        if total + len(s) > 4096:
            break
        out += s
        total += len(s)

    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: ASCII string (NUL-terminated when used as C string).
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR for the data payload to nsock_write.
# The stub may pass datalen = -1 (treat as C-string) or a non-negative length.
# Our goal: Produce interesting but valid ASCII strings that exercise different
# behaviors: empty, small, large, with newlines, CRLF, long runs, mixed whitespace,
# printable edge chars, format-like strings, and typical protocol lines.

PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))  # space..~
SAFE_ASCII = PRINTABLE

PROTO_TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    # HTTP request lines and headers
    "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: example.com\r\nUser-Agent: nsock-fuzz\r\n\r\n",
    "POST /submit HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello",
    # SMTP-like
    "HELO example.com\r\nMAIL FROM:<a@b>\r\nRCPT TO:<c@d>\r\nDATA\r\nSubject: Test\r\n\r\nBody\r\n.\r\n",
    # TLS-ish ClientHello as ASCII hex (still ASCII text)
    "16 03 01 00 2e 01 00 00 2a 03 03 00 00 00 00\n",
    # Simple lines
    "line1\nline2\nline3\n",
    # Mixed CRLF/LF
    "a\r\nb\nc\r\n",
]

FORMAT_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "%s",
    "%d %u %x %p",
    "%-20s %08x %*.*s",
    "%1$s %2$d %3$#x",
    "100%% done\n",
]

WORDS: List[str] = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon",
    "lorem", "ipsum", "dolor", "sit", "amet",
]


def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _repeat_char_run(rng: random.Random, chs: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    ch = rng.choice(chs)
    ln = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ch * ln


def _join_words(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    return ' '.join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(count))


def _edge_cases() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "",  # empty
        "\n",  # single LF
        "\r\n",  # CRLF
        " ",  # single space
        "\t",  # tab
        "~",  # highest ASCII printable
        "!",  # punctuation
    ]


def _build_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []

    # Edge cases
    cands.extend(_edge_cases())

    # Repeated characters and runs
    cands.append(_repeat_char_run(rng, "A0 ", 1, 64))
    cands.append(_repeat_char_run(rng, "\n\r ", 1, 64))

    # Random printable of various lengths
    for ln in [1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1023]:
        # Keep total <= 4096; we still provide variety
        cands.append(_rand_printable(rng, min(ln, 1024)))

    # Lines with CRLF and LF combinations
    cands.append("header1: v1\r\nheader2: v2\r\n\r\n")
    cands.append("one\n")

    # Format-like strings
    cands.extend(FORMAT_STRINGS)

    # Protocol-ish strings
    cands.extend(PROTO_TEMPLATES)

    # Words joined
    cands.append(_join_words(rng, rng.randint(2, 20)))

    # Mixed whitespace and printable edges
    cands.append("\t" + _rand_printable(rng, 20) + "\n")

    # Longish payload near 512 to influence modulo in stub
    long_near_512 = _rand_printable(rng, 600)
    cands.append(long_near_512)

    # Payload exactly 512, 513 for boundary behavior after modulo
    cands.append(_rand_printable(rng, 512))
    cands.append(_rand_printable(rng, 513))

    return cands


def _choose_candidate(rng: random.Random, cands: List[str]) -> str:
    # Weighted choice to cover: empty, small, medium, large, structured
    idx = rng.randrange(len(cands))
    s = cands[idx]
    # Occasionally augment with suffix/prefix to vary endings
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.2:
        s += "\r\n"
    elif roll < 0.35:
        s += "\n"
    elif roll < 0.45:
        s = ""  # produce empty sometimes
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    candidates = _build_candidates(rng)
    s = _choose_candidate(rng, candidates)

    # Ensure ASCII printable plus common control chars LF/CR/TAB only
    # Replace any accidental out-of-range (should not occur) just in case
    filtered = []
    for ch in s:
        oc = ord(ch)
        if ch in ("\n", "\r", "\t") or 32 <= oc <= 126:
            filtered.append(ch)
        else:
            filtered.append(' ')  # normalize
    s = ''.join(filtered)

    # Truncate to 4096 bytes max
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]

    # Return bytes without a NUL terminator; the fuzzing harness will store
    # this as the content backing FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string). When the stub
    # passes datalen = -1, nsock_write will treat c_str() as NUL-terminated
    # because std::string ensures that.
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

import random
import secrets
from typing import List

# Generator for nsock proxy chain description strings
# The fuzz stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a NUL-terminated string.
# We will return bytes that represent such a string (without the trailing NUL; the fuzzer will handle C-string semantics).
# The string should be valid and parseable by nsock_proxychain_new. We craft realistic proxy URIs and chains.

SCHEMES = [
    "socks4",
    "socks5",
    "socks5h",  # common alias for hostname resolution via proxy
    "http",
    "https",
    "connect",  # HTTP CONNECT style (sometimes synonymous with http)
]

HOSTS = [
    "127.0.0.1",
    "::1",
    "localhost",
    "proxy.local",
    "example.com",
    "intranet",
    "10.0.0.1",
    "192.168.1.1",
]

USERS = [
    "user",
    "admin",
    "guest",
    "alice",
    "bob",
    "",
]

PASSWORDS = [
    "pass",
    "password",
    "secret",
    "toor",
    "p@ss:word",  # include a colon to test URL parsing and escaping behavior
    "",
]

# Some ports of interest
PORTS = [1080, 1081, 9050, 3128, 8080, 8000, 443, 80, 22, 53]

# Optional parameters sometimes supported by proxy chain grammars
# We include flags that are commonly seen in tools: tls, verify, sni, alpn, udp, timeout, ipv4/ipv6, noauth
PARAM_KEYS = [
    "tls",
    "verify",
    "sni",
    "alpn",
    "udp",
    "timeout",
    "ipv4",
    "ipv6",
    "noauth",
]

ALPN_OPTIONS = ["h2", "http/1.1", "spdy/3"]

# Separators between chained proxies vary by implementation. We include a few commonly used ones.
CHAIN_SEPARATORS = [",", ";", " ", "|", "->"]

# Some implementations accept brackets for IPv6 literals and credentials in URI authority form.

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p


def _rand_port(r: random.Random) -> int:
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.8):
        return r.choice(PORTS)
    return r.randint(1, 65535)


def _maybe_credentials(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.6):
        user = r.choice(USERS)
        pwd = r.choice(PASSWORDS)
        if user == "" and pwd == "":
            return ""
        if pwd == "":
            return f"{user}@"
        if user == "":
            # Some grammars may not like missing user with only password, so include user if empty
            user = "user"
        return f"{user}:{pwd}@"
    return ""


def _host_for_scheme(r: random.Random, scheme: str) -> str:
    host = r.choice(HOSTS)
    # Wrap IPv6 literal in brackets when paired with port
    if ":" in host and not host.startswith("["):
        return f"[{host}]"
    return host


def _params_for_scheme(r: random.Random, scheme: str) -> List[str]:
    params = []
    # Generic flags
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.3):
        params.append("tls=1")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        params.append("verify=0")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.25):
        # Use a sensible SNI hostname
        params.append(f"sni={r.choice(['example.com','service.local','target'])}")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        params.append(f"alpn={r.choice(ALPN_OPTIONS)}")
    if scheme.startswith("socks") and _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        params.append("udp=1")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.35):
        params.append(f"timeout={r.randint(100, 60000)}")
    # Mutually exclusive IP families sometimes supported
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.15):
        params.append("ipv4")
    elif _rand_bool(r, 0.15):
        params.append("ipv6")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.15):
        params.append("noauth")
    return params


def _one_proxy_uri(r: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = r.choice(SCHEMES)
    creds = _maybe_credentials(r)
    host = _host_for_scheme(r, scheme)
    port = _rand_port(r)

    # Some grammars accept scheme://user:pass@host:port;others accept scheme:user:pass@host:port
    use_slashes = _rand_bool(r, 0.7)
    sep = "://" if use_slashes else ":"

    # Optionally include path-like suffix or query-like parameters after host:port
    params = _params_for_scheme(r, scheme)
    suffix = ""
    if params:
        # Many grammars accept ;key=val or ?key=val&key2=val2; include both styles occasionally
        style = r.choice([";", "?", ";?"])
        if style == ";":
            suffix = ";" + ";".join(params)
        elif style == "?":
            # Join with & for query
            suffix = "?" + "&".join(params)
        else:
            # Mixed style for broader coverage
            half = len(params) // 2 or 1
            suffix = ";" + ";".join(params[:half]) + "?" + "&".join(params[half:])

    return f"{scheme}{sep}{creds}{host}:{port}{suffix}"


def _chain(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose number of proxies in chain: 1 to 4, skew toward multi-hop
    n = 1 + int(r.random() ** 0.6 * 3)  # bias towards higher values within 1..4
    parts = [_one_proxy_uri(r) for _ in range(n)]
    # Optionally include per-hop whitespace trimming and varying separators
    if n == 1:
        return parts[0]
    # Build with mixed separators sometimes
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        sep = r.choice(CHAIN_SEPARATORS)
        return sep.join(parts)
    else:
        out = []
        for i, p in enumerate(parts):
            out.append(p)
            if i + 1 < n:
                out.append(r.choice(CHAIN_SEPARATORS))
        return "".join(out)


def _global_options(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Some grammars allow leading global options, e.g., mode=random, try=DNS first, or overall timeout
    opts = []
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.25):
        opts.append(f"mode={r.choice(['random','strict','balanced'])}")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.25):
        opts.append(f"resolve={r.choice(['local','proxy'])}")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        opts.append(f"retries={r.randint(0,5)}")
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        opts.append(f"maxtime={r.randint(1000,120000)}")
    return opts


def _compose_full_description(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Combine optional global options and chains. Some implementations use a newline or a prefix keyword.
    desc = _chain(r)
    opts = _global_options(r)
    if opts and _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        # Prepend as a header-like directive line
        directive = r.choice(["options:", "global:", "config:", "set:"])
        # Key-value pairs separated by spaces or commas
        kv_sep = r.choice([" ", ","]) 
        header = directive + kv_sep + kv_sep.join(opts)
        joiner = "\n" if _rand_bool(r, 0.6) else ";"
        desc = header + joiner + desc
    elif opts:
        # Append options at the end separated by a delimiter
        joiner = r.choice([";", "\n", " "])
        desc = desc + joiner + " ".join(opts)

    # Optionally include comments or whitespace that many parsers tolerate
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.3):
        comment = r.choice(["# chain for testing", "// proxy chain", "# autogenerated"])
        # Put comment at end or on its own line
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
            desc = desc + " " + comment
        else:
            desc = comment + "\n" + desc

    # Trim to ensure overall size bound when encoded to bytes
    if len(desc) > 4000:
        desc = desc[:4000]
    return desc


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """Generate a valid proxy chain description as bytes.

    The output is designed to be a parseable configuration string for nsock_proxychain_new,
    covering multiple schemes, credentials, IPv4/IPv6 hosts, ports, parameters, and chaining styles.
    The result is ASCII/UTF-8 byte sequence without an explicit NUL terminator (the fuzzing harness
    provides C-string semantics). The length is kept <= 4096 bytes.
    """
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally craft very short or very long, but still valid, inputs
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.15:
        # Minimal single proxy
        scheme = r.choice(SCHEMES)
        host = _host_for_scheme(r, scheme)
        port = _rand_port(r)
        s = f"{scheme}://{host}:{port}"
    elif choice < 0.3:
        # Credentials-focused
        s = _one_proxy_uri(r)
        # Ensure credentials present
        if "@" not in s:
            # inject credentials before host
            scheme_end = s.find("://")
            if scheme_end == -1:
                scheme_end = s.find(":")
            if scheme_end != -1:
                prefix = s[:scheme_end]
                rest = s[scheme_end:]
                s = f"{prefix}://user:pass@" + rest.lstrip(":/")
    else:
        s = _compose_full_description(r)

    # Optional trailing newline or whitespace
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.3):
        s += "\n"
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        s = s.strip()  # normalize sometimes

    # Ensure size limit
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
